§10.4.1 Blanks Inside Sentences

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

forms-blanks-inside-sentences · forms

✅ Normative

A sentence with fill-in gaps MUST be kept intact, with each gap rendered as [blank] at its printed position. A hint printed with a blank MUST be kept next to that blank, once.

Affidavits, declarations and notarial blocks print their fields as prose with gaps in it:

The Enterprise is ______________% Black Owned using the flow-through principle …
Executed on the (date) ______ day of (month) ____________ (year) ________

The Enterprise is [blank]% Black Owned using the flow-through principle …
Executed on the *(date)* [blank] day of *(month)* [blank] *(year)* [blank]

Fill-Ins§10.4.4 assumes a label followed by a field. Here there is no label — the sentence is the label, and one sentence can hold three blanks. The sentence MUST NOT be broken up into key-value lines, and a key MUST NOT be made up from the words before a blank.

The sub-cases

The page prints Output
A blank inside a sentence [blank] in its printed position
A hint inside or beside the blank The hint as printed, next to its own blank, once
A caption under the line The caption kept with that blank, once, never duplicated
A currency glyph before a blank $[blank], keeping the printed spacing

✅ Sample — blanks inside bulleted sentences

Each bullet is a sentence with one percentage blank in it; the indented group prints a short label, =, then the blank. The page also carries a three-row table whose last column is an unlabelled tick box.

✅ Sample — hints printed inside the blanks

Executed on the (date) ___ day of (month) ___ (year) ___: the hints sit before each blank, in blue italic. Print Your Name: and Your Signature: are ordinary labelled fill-ins; the (If any) hint of Lawyer Signature: stays beside its blank.

✅ Sample — captions printed under the line

A notarial block where the caption is set in small capitals beneath each dotted line — NAME, DATE, SIGNATURE OF DEPONENT — and a fee line that prints $ before its blank. A standalone line takes its caption as its label, with no colon because the two sit on different lines; the NAME line inside the sentence keeps its caption right after its blank.
